1. d5+ {The pawn gives check. (a) NOTE: In the present position the game must come to a drawn-
game, because your king will be no more capable of going forwards towards your pawn, supposing
always that your adversary plays all his moves with exactness.} Kd7 {The king, at his queen's
second square.} 2. Kd4 {The king, at his queen's fourth square.} Bg3 {The bishop, at the adverse
king's knight's third square.} 3. Ra1 {The rook, at its queen's rook's square.} Bf4 {The bishop,
at the adverse king's bishop's fourth square. (b) NOTE: It is material for him to keep his
bishop at some distance from your king, to enable himself to give check, in case you should play
the king to one of the black squares next to your pawn.} 4. Ra7+ {The rook gives check.} Kd6
{The king, at his queen's third square. (c) NOTE: If he had covered the check, you would have
won the game, by pushing your king forwards to the black square facing his bishop.} 5. Ke4 {The
king, at his fourth square.} Bg3 {The bishop, at the adverse king's knight's third square. (d)
NOTE: If he had played his bishop to your king's rook's second square, you would have won the
game, by playing your rook to his king's knight's second square. It is to be observed, that, in
the defence of that party, the bishop must never be far distant from the adverse king.} 6. Re7
{The rook, at the adverse king's.knight's second square.} Be1 {The bishop, at the adverse king's
square, to give check.} 7. Rd7+ {The rook gives check.} Kxd7 {The king, at his queen's second
square.} 8. d6 {The pawn, one move. (e) NOTE: If you had advanced your king, he would have
obliged you to retrograde, by a check given with his bishop.} Kc6 {The king, at his queen's
bishop's third square. (f) NOTE: If he had made any other move, he would have lost the game.} 9.
Ke5 {The king, at the adverse king's fourth square.} Bb4 {The bishop, at the adverse queen's
knight's fourth square. (g) NOTE: In this position your pawn is forced as your king can no more
go forwards, without covering your rook.} 10. d7 {The pawn, one move, giving check to the rook.}
Kxd7 {The king takes the pawn.} 11. Kd5 {The king, at the adverse queen's fourth square.} Kc7
{The king, at his queen's bishop's second square. (h) NOTE: When one remains with a bishop
against a rook, he must as soon as possible bring his king into that corner of the chess-board
that is not of the same colour with the bishop. It is the only place where he can be sure of a
back-game.} *
</script></div>
